configurePresets.name: base
configurePresets.description: Shared base preset, inherited by the real ones. RESEARCH: (a) what does `hidden` actually do, mechanically? (b) what schema `version` do you need — check the cmake-presets(7) version-to-feature table — and what breaks if you pick too low? (c) when does inheritance hurt readability vs help it? (d) why does this schema have BOTH `environment` and `cacheVariables` — what belongs in each?

configurePresets.name: debug
configurePresets.description: RESEARCH: what *should* actually differ between Debug and Release builds? Think about: optimization level (-O0 vs -O2/-O3), debug info (-g, -g3, split-dwarf), assertions (NDEBUG), sanitizers (asan/ubsan/tsan/msan — which combine, which conflict), LTO, frame pointers. Decide before you fill cacheVariables.

configurePresets.name: release
configurePresets.description: TODO: same exercise as debug — what does a release build need? Also research the OTHER two standard build types: RelWithDebInfo and MinSizeRel. When would you reach for those instead?

buildPresets.name: debug
buildPresets.description: RESEARCH: do you actually need a buildPreset, or is `cmake --build build/debug` already enough? What do the `jobs`, `targets`, `configuration`, `cleanFirst` fields buy you? When does `configuration` matter at build time (hint: multi-config generators like Xcode/VS behave differently from Ninja here)?

testPresets.name: debug
testPresets.description: RESEARCH: testPresets drive `ctest --preset <name>`. You'll need enable_testing() and some add_test()/gtest_discover_tests calls in CMakeLists.txt before this does anything. Pick a test framework (GoogleTest? Catch2? doctest?) and decide how to pull it in (find_package vs FetchContent vs CPM vs vcpkg) — each has real tradeoffs.

_NOTES_TO_SELF._about_this_field: JSON doesn't support comments, so this object exists only as a scratchpad for research prompts. CMake should ignore unknown top-level keys; if it warns, move these notes into per-preset `description` fields and delete this block.
_NOTES_TO_SELF._ccache: TODO: wire ccache in. Two common places: (1) here in cacheVariables on `base` — set CMAKE_C_COMPILER_LAUNCHER and CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_LAUNCHER to "ccache". (2) inside CMakeLists.txt with find_program(CCACHE_PROGRAM ccache) + set(CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_LAUNCHER ...). Read both approaches. Question to answer: what happens when both are set, and which scope do you actually want for a project that other people might clone?
_NOTES_TO_SELF._clang_tidy: TODO: decide whether clang-tidy runs automatically on every build (CMAKE_CXX_CLANG_TIDY) or only on demand (separate CI step / pre-commit). The first is more thorough but slower and noisier; the second is easier to ignore. Pick one consciously.
_NOTES_TO_SELF._warnings: TODO: your CMakeLists.txt currently uses add_compile_options(-Wall -Wextra ...). Research why that's considered the wrong place for warnings in modern CMake. Hint: target_compile_options + a small interface library is the idiomatic answer. Also: those flags are GCC/Clang-only — what's the cross-compiler way?
